# E07 — Quaternary landscapes, sea levels and environments

**Window:** Quaternary–Holocene; modern processes continue.

**Question:** How did shorelines, wetlands, rivers and habitats change before and during human occupation?

## Evidence presently available in this seed

The repository has not yet assembled a critically reviewed local sea-level or palaeoenvironmental series. This is an explicitly open dossier, not a filled gap.

Source routes: [S025](../sources/S025.md), [S042](../sources/S042.md).

## What this does not establish

The present beach, backwaters and river mouths must not be treated as stationary. A single flood story is not a complete coastal history. Do not give unsourced dates to the birth of a lagoon or the destruction of a port.

## Research tasks

- [ ] Inventory dated cores, pollen, charcoal, sedimentary facies and geomorphological studies.
- [ ] Separate global sea-level context from measured local relative sea level.
- [ ] Record reservoir corrections, sediment reworking and age-depth model uncertainty.
- [ ] Retrieve a versioned chronostratigraphic chart before importing formal numerical boundaries.
- [ ] Cross-link later flood accounts to independent sedimentary evidence without presuming agreement.
